finding: The calibration_plot PROC SQL translates mean(pd_logistic) and mean(default_flag) with bare polars .sum() (_sum_pd, _defaults). S10 forbids bare .sum() for PROC SQL aggregates. The same file uses sql_sum/sql_min/sql_max for decile_analysis (:166-169), so S10 is applied inconsistently. For an all-missing group (the null pred_bin when pd_logistic is missing), bare sum gives 0, so mean_predicted prints 0.0000 where SAS prints an empty field (verified: null bin -> 0.0 vs sql_mean -> null). Inventory rows 136-138 predate S10 and spell .sum().
cites: RULEBOOK §2 PROC SQL aggregates row (S10: 'never bare polars .sum()'); metrics_calculation.sas:310-311; inventory.tsv:136-138
fix: _sum_pd=sas_compat.sql_sum(pl.col('pd_logistic')), _defaults=sas_compat.sql_sum(pl.col('default_flag')). Better still, use sas_compat.sql_mean directly for mean_predicted / mean_actual (see B-03).

finding: The SQL mean() translations divide by pl.len() (count(*)), but SAS mean divides by the count of NON-MISSING values. This affects default_rate=defaults/total_count and avg_pd=pd_sum/total_count (:173-175), and mean_predicted / mean_actual = sum/bin_count (:293-294). With a missing default_flag in a group, Python gives 1/3 where SAS gives 1/2 (verified). Not reachable on judged inputs: default_flag and pd are never missing.
cites: metrics_calculation.sas:197-198,310-311 (mean); RULEBOOK §2 S10 (sql_mean) vs A7; inventory.tsv:125,137 ('SAS mean ignores missing')
fix: Divide by pl.col(x).count() (the non-missing count) inside the agg, or use sas_compat.sql_mean(x) in the agg. Both keep the division after aggregation (A7).

finding: cum_bad = flag(default_flag != 0).cum_sum() is not SAS's else branch. In SAS, 'if default_flag = 0 then cum_good + 1; else cum_bad + 1;' sends a MISSING default_flag to the else branch and counts it as bad. In Python, null != 0 is null, flag() maps it to 0, and the row is never counted. Verified on [0, ., 1, 0]: Python [0,0,1,1], SAS [0,1,2,2]. This changes ks_value, KS_Statistic and KS_Cutoff when default_flag is missing.
cites: metrics_calculation.sas:96-97; RULEBOOK §2 if/else row (one when/otherwise chain, first-match order); inventory.tsv:107 ('cum_bad = cumulative count of everything else (:96-97, else branch)')

finding: The KS remerge filter compares ks_value == max with a plain polars ==. When every ks_value is missing (validation set with only one class: total_bad_count or total_good_count = 0, so cum_pct_* is missing), max is missing. SAS's where ks_value = . is TRUE, so it keeps every row: KS_Statistic missing, one KS_Cutoff per row. Python keeps 0 rows. Verified: 3 rows of one class give Python 0 rows and sas_compat.eq 3 rows. ks_value is MISSING_NULLABLE on that path, so the helper is mandatory there.
cites: metrics_calculation.sas:110; RULEBOOK §2 comparison row (A2: helpers mandatory where the operand can be missing; sas_compat.eq '. = . is true'); RULEBOOK §2 PROC SQL remerge row
fix: ks_calculation.filter(sas_compat.eq(pl.col('ks_value'), pl.lit(max_ks_value.item(0, 0), pl.Float64))). Or record why ks_value is never missing in the inventory and keep the plain ==.

finding: The INTO emulation float(sas_compat.sas_best(x, 8)) raises ValueError when the SQL aggregate is missing: sas_best(None) returns '', and float('') fails. This happens on an empty input: sql_sum over 0 rows is null. SAS stores the missing value in the macro variable and the later divisions (:99-100, :232-233) give missing. The same pattern is at :105, :216 and :217-219. Python crashes instead (verified). Unreachable on receivable inputs (>= 3,000 rows).
cites: RULEBOOK §2 select into row (A9); RULEBOOK §2 PROC SQL aggregates row (S10: missing over zero rows); metrics_calculation.sas:80-84,213-217
fix: Map a missing aggregate to None before float(): v = sas_compat.sas_best(x, 8); total = float(v) if v else None. sas_compat.div already returns missing for a None divisor.
